q: Which of the following is an example of a system message?
opts: What time do you open on Sunday?
You are a cheerful assistant for a bike shop. Only answer questions about bikes and repairs.
exp: A system message sets the assistant's role, tone and rules, such as being a cheerful bike shop assistant that only discusses bikes. The opening-hours question is a user message, the JSON is a parameter setting, and gpt-5-mini is a model name.

q: Your app must always receive JSON that matches a specific schema. Besides describing the format in the prompt, which feature helps enforce it?
opts: Structured outputs with a JSON schema
exp: Structured outputs let you pass a JSON schema with the request so that the model's response follows that schema, which is more reliable than instructions alone. A higher temperature makes output more random, stop sequences only end output at a marker, and image detail applies to image input.

q: For each of the following statements about prompts, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: The model receives the system message only once, when the model is deployed.
A prompt can contain instructions, context and examples.
Asking the model to answer in a specific language usually works.
exp: No for the first: the system message is part of each request, not something stored in the deployment. Yes for the second: prompts often combine instructions, background content and examples. Yes for the third: modern language models follow instructions such as 'answer in French' well.

q: Match each problem with a chat solution to the prompt change that fixes it best. Each fix can be used once or not at all.
items: Answers come back in the wrong format
Answers include facts that are not in the provided documents
The tone of answers changes from one reply to the next
targets: Tell the model to use only the provided documents
Define a persona and tone in the system message
Show an example of the required format
exp: A length limit controls long answers, an example of the format fixes formatting, restricting answers to the provided documents reduces unsupported facts, and a persona with a defined tone keeps the style consistent. Quota controls throughput and does not change the content of answers.

q: Why is it useful to put user-supplied text between delimiters, such as triple quotes or <text> tags, in a prompt?
opts: It reduces the token cost to zero
It is required syntax for every prompt
It helps the model tell your instructions apart from the content it should process
exp: Delimiters clearly mark where the content starts and ends, so the model treats it as material to work on rather than as instructions, which improves accuracy and helps against prompt injection. Delimiters do not encrypt text or remove token costs, and they are a best practice, not mandatory syntax.

q: Complete the sentences about prompt instructions.
tpl: Adding 'If you are not sure, say that you don't know' helps reduce {0}. Adding 'Respond in fewer than 50 words' controls the {1} of the answer.
exp: Allowing the model to admit uncertainty reduces hallucinations, because it no longer feels it must invent an answer. A word limit controls the length of the response. Latency and cost per token are not changed by these instructions, and data residency depends on the deployment type, not the prompt.

q: For a customer service chat solution, which TWO items belong in the system message rather than in a user message? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opts: Rules about which topics the assistant may discuss
The order number that the customer typed
exp: The system message holds instructions that apply to the whole conversation, such as allowed topics and the assistant's persona and tone. The customer's question, the order number they typed and their greeting are part of the conversation, so they belong in user messages.

q: Which line is a safety instruction that you might add to a system message?
opts: If a user asks for harmful or dangerous content, politely refuse and do not provide it.
exp: Safety system message instructions tell the model how to handle harmful requests, for example by refusing politely, and they work together with content filters. Tone, language and formatting instructions shape the style of answers but do not address safety.

q: What is prompt engineering?
opts: Designing and refining prompts to get better results from a model
Building the GPUs that run models
Training a new model from scratch
Writing SQL queries for a database
exp: Prompt engineering is the practice of writing and improving prompts, with clear instructions, context, examples and output formats, so a model produces more accurate and useful responses. It does not involve hardware, training a new model or writing database queries.

q: After you deploy several models in a Foundry project, where can you see all of them with their names and settings?
opts: The list of model deployments in the project
exp: The project's list of model deployments shows each deployment with its name, model, version and deployment type, and you can open it to test or edit it. Azure Marketplace sells offerings, Entra ID manages identities, and Azure DevOps manages code and pipelines.

q: Which value do you copy from the Foundry portal into your app's configuration so that the Foundry SDK can connect to your project?
opts: The URL of the portal home page
exp: The project endpoint, in the form https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>, is what AIProjectClient needs. The billing ID, tenant name and portal home page URL do not identify the project's API.

q: For each of the following statements about model deployments, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: Deploying a model copies the model weights to your laptop.
Each deployment can use its own content filter configuration.
You can deploy the same model more than once under different names.
Deleting a deployment stops apps that call it from working.
exp: No for the first: the model runs in Azure, and your app calls its endpoint. Yes for the second: content filter configurations are assigned per deployment. Yes for the third: deployment names are unique, so the same model can be deployed several times with different settings. Yes for the fourth: apps that call a deleted deployment get errors.

q: You wrote two versions of a system message and want to know which gives better answers. What is the most reliable approach in Foundry?
opts: Ask one colleague which version they prefer
Check which version costs less on the bill
Run an evaluation for each version with the same test dataset and compare the scores
exp: Evaluations score responses on a test dataset with metrics such as relevance and groundedness, so running both versions against the same data gives an objective comparison. A single opinion is anecdotal, cost does not measure quality, and quota only affects throughput.

q: Match each question to the evaluator that answers it. Each evaluator can be used once or not at all.
items: Is the answer supported by the provided context?
Does the answer address the user's question?
Is the language natural and easy to read?
Does the answer contain violent content?
exp: Groundedness checks support in the context, relevance checks whether the question is answered, fluency checks language quality, and risk and safety evaluators such as violence detect harmful content. Latency measures speed and is not a quality or safety evaluator for answer content.

q: Which TWO actions can you perform in the Foundry chat playground? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
opts: Move the resource to another Azure region
exp: The playground lets you change the instructions and request parameters and immediately see the effect on responses. It does not retrain models, change their weights or move resources between regions; those require fine-tuning or redeploying resources.

q: Complete the sentences about deploying models in Microsoft Foundry.
tpl: You create a deployment by selecting a model in the {0}. The number of tokens the deployment can process is limited by its {1}.
exp: Models are chosen and deployed from the model catalog. Standard deployments receive a tokens-per-minute quota, which limits throughput. The activity log and Azure Advisor do not deploy models, and storage tiers and virtual machine sizes do not apply to Foundry-hosted standard deployments.

q: A chat response ends early and its finish reason is content_filter. What does this mean?
opts: The model reached the maximum number of tokens
The output was stopped because the content filter flagged it
The deployment's quota is used up
exp: A finish reason of content_filter means the generated content was flagged by the content filtering system and was cut off or omitted. Hitting the token limit gives the finish reason length, exhausted quota returns a 429 error, and a deleted deployment returns an error rather than a partial response.

q: You want to check, without code, whether a deployed vision-capable model can describe a product photo. What should you use?
opts: The chat playground with the photo attached
exp: The chat playground lets you attach an image to a message and send it to a vision-capable deployment to see how the model describes it. Azure Monitor shows metrics, cost analysis shows spending and Key Vault stores secrets; none of them send prompts to a model.

q: Which command installs the packages that a Python chat client needs to connect to a Foundry project with Microsoft Entra ID?
exp: azure-ai-projects provides AIProjectClient and azure-identity provides DefaultAzureCredential, so a Python chat client installs both with pip. npm is for JavaScript packages, azure-storage-queue is for storage queues, and python-ai is not an Azure SDK package.

q: Where should a chat client keep the project endpoint instead of hard-coding it in the source code?
opts: In an environment variable or app configuration setting
exp: Storing the endpoint in an environment variable or configuration lets you change environments without editing code, which is standard practice. A comment is not read by the program, the system message is sent to the model rather than used to connect, and you cannot put configuration in a model's training data.

q: Complete the Python code that gives the model an instruction for the whole request and prints the answer.
tpl:
response = openai.responses.create(
    model="support-chat",
    {0}="You are a concise assistant. Answer in one sentence.",
    input=question,
)
print(response.{1})
exp: The Responses API accepts an instructions parameter that works like a system message, and the generated text is in output_text. There is no system or role parameter on responses.create(), and content and text_output are not properties of the response object.

q: For each of the following statements about the Foundry SDK, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: responses.create() always requires a temperature value.
get_openai_client() returns a client that can call deployed models.
With Microsoft Entra ID authentication, the app does not need to store an API key.
exp: Yes for the first: the endpoint identifies the project. No for the second: temperature is optional and has a default. Yes for the third: the returned OpenAI-compatible client sends requests to your deployments. Yes for the fourth: Entra ID tokens replace keys, so no secret has to be stored.

q: Your chat client runs in Azure App Service. Which way of authenticating to the Foundry project avoids storing any secret?
opts: An API key in the source code
A password in the system message
A managed identity used through DefaultAzureCredential
exp: A managed identity gives the App Service its own Entra ID identity, and DefaultAzureCredential picks it up automatically, so no secret is stored; the identity still needs a role on the project. Keys in code and passwords in prompts can leak, and anonymous access is not allowed.

q: Match each HTTP error from a chat client to its most likely cause. Each cause can be used once or not at all.
targets: The deployment name or endpoint is wrong
The identity has no role that allows the call
exp: 401 means the caller could not be authenticated, often because of a missing or invalid credential. 403 means the identity is known but lacks permission, such as a missing role. 404 usually means the deployment or endpoint path does not exist. 429 means the rate limit was reached. An oversized image would return a different validation error.

q: A long chat is close to the model's context window. Which TWO approaches keep requests within the limit? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
opts: Keep sending the full history forever
Summarize older turns and send the summary instead
Drop the oldest messages but keep the system message
Add more few-shot examples on every turn
exp: Summarizing older turns or dropping the oldest messages, while keeping the system message, reduces the tokens sent and keeps the conversation inside the context window. Sending everything will eventually exceed the limit, temperature does not change length, and extra examples add more tokens.

q: Your app must log how many input and output tokens each model call used, to track cost. Where does it find these numbers?
opts: In the usage property of the response
exp: Model responses include a usage object with the number of input and output tokens, plus a total, which the app can log for cost tracking. The deployment name identifies the model, the status code reports success or failure, and the system message is part of the request.

q: You are building a console chat that uses the Responses API. Put the steps in the correct order. Not every step is used.
items: Read the user's input from the console
Create the project client and get the OpenAI client
Call responses.create() with the input and the previous response ID
Print output_text and remember this response's ID
Delete the deployment after each turn
exp: The clients are created once at the start. Each turn then reads the input, calls responses.create() with previous_response_id so the conversation continues, prints the answer and saves the new response ID for the next turn. Deleting the deployment would break the app.

q: What does DefaultAzureCredential do in a chat client?
opts: It tries several sign-in methods, such as environment settings, a managed identity and the Azure CLI, to get a token
It stores your password in the source code
It creates a new Azure subscription
It generates a new API key
exp: DefaultAzureCredential checks a chain of credential sources, including environment variables, managed identity and developer sign-ins such as the Azure CLI, and uses the first one that works to get a Microsoft Entra token. It does not store passwords, create subscriptions or generate API keys.

q: Complete the sentence about the packages for a Python chat client.
tpl: A lightweight Foundry chat client in Python uses {0} to connect to the project and {1} to authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID.
exp: azure-ai-projects provides the project client that also gives you an OpenAI-compatible client, and azure-identity provides credentials such as DefaultAzureCredential. The storage, Key Vault, Cosmos DB and Event Hubs packages serve other Azure services.
